pairs.reason: Classification and CrawlError intentionally share the page-outcome Literal prefix; the test_crawl_error_members_derive_from_classification invariant pins the shared members and the documented pipeline-only additions.

_default_http_fetcher and _default_cffi_fetcher are two implementations of one security contract, and both docstrings say so: SSRF-safe manual redirect handling (F1) and sensitive-header stripping on cross-domain redirects (Fix 3). The mirroring is deliberate, so this is sanctioned rather than collapsed -- but it is also the most expensive duplication in the tree, because two bodies have to stay in step for a redirect rule to hold on both transports, and the only thing keeping them in step is a comment. Fold the redirect loop into one helper the two fetchers call; until then the guard is the shared signature every concrete fetcher must keep, which is what a fold would have to preserve.

Tavily, Brave and Serper each parse the body, test the status, raise SearchProviderError and then funnel into _collect_results. The error contract is repeated per provider where one shared parse-and-check would do, so the three sites can drift apart silently: a provider can start reporting a different message or stop funnelling and the other two say nothing. Sanctioned so the repetition stays visible until it is folded into a single helper all three call; the guard is the error the providers must keep raising, with its detail intact.
